text: In this study, SO was used to chemically modify the commonly used leveling agent polydimethyldiallylammonium (PD) in through-hole electroplating, resulting in a more effective leveling agent, PDS, which improved the throwing power (TP), leading to through-hole circuit boards with better metal coverage in difficult-to-reach areas. Furthermore, theoretical and experimental studies were conducted to understand how the −SO structure influences the leveling ability of the leveling agent. The study demonstrates that the −SO - modified additive significantly enhances the copper plating process, resulting in thicker and more uniform deposits in through-holes, which are critical for ensuring high-quality circuit boards.Additionally, this study elu cidates the mechanism of action of the leveling agent on the copper surface, providing theoretical support for the development of copper plating leveling agents. The leveling ability differences between the leveling agents PD and PDS were investigated using Cyclic Voltammetry, constant current method, and Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy. Additionally, the optimal concentrations of the additives were determined. Quantum chemical calculations were employed to analyze the electrostatic potential, HOMO/LUMO orbitals, and differential charge density on the Cu (111) surface for both leveling agents. These theoretical analyses provided insights into the reasons behind the differing leveling abilities of the two agents.

text: With the rapid development of the electronics industry, an increasing number of consumer products, such as computers, electronic watches, wearable devices, smartphones, and communication equipment, are becoming more intelligent, lightweight, and miniaturized[1–3]. In these advanced electronic products, the Printed Circuit Board (PCB) is a critical component, serving as the main conduit between various electronic elements, enabling them to connect and work together in a coordinated manner. The metallization of PCBs, which enables the interconnection of electronic components, is particularly crucial[4,5]. Through-hole electroplating plays a vital role in this process, with copper electroplating emerging as the mainstream choice for PCB interconnection due to its excellent conductivity and low cost[6]. However, current copper electroplating technology faces challenges in meeting the ever-increasing demands of PCB manufacturing, which has become a bottleneck limiting the improvement of PCB performance [7,8].Therefore, the preparation of high-quality through-hole plating and high-density interconnect circuit boards holds significant industrial and economic importance[9].

text: Currently, the most widely used technology in the through-hole plating process of circuit boards is acid copper plating, which typically involves a conventional acid copper plating solution containing copper sulfate, sulfuric acid, and trace amounts of plating additives[10]. Traditional electroplating additives can be categorized into suppressors, accelerators, and levelers[11–13]. In the context of through-hole electroplating, the key substance capable of enhancing the TP value is the leveler, which, as a crucial component in the acid copper plating solution, requires only a small addition to effectively increase the TP value [14,15]. As a critical metric for assessing the performance of throughhole copper plating, the TP value is calculated as the ratio of the copper thickness on the surface to the copper layer thickness inside the hole [16]. The traditional calculation method is divided into six-point method[17,18], and the specific measurement method is described in detail later.

Quantum chemical calculations of the HOMO/LUMO orbitals and molecular dy namics simulation methods were employed to explain the synergistic interaction between PBDGE and Cl - on the electrode surface, investi gating the reasons behind its ability to enhance cathodic polarization. Zheng et al.[2,20] copolymerized 1-vinyl imidazole with 1, 4-butanediol diglycidyl ether to obtain poly (1-vinyl imidazole co 1, 4-butanediol diglycidyl ether) (VIBDGE). Electroplating experiments confirmed that at the optimal VIBDGE concentration, the TP of through-hole plating increased by 43.62 %. Quantum chemical calculations indicated that VIBDGE has a strong electron-donating ability, allowing it to provide electrons to low-energy vacant orbitals during the copper deposition process, thereby forming covalent bonds. text: After adding different leveling agents in the VMS, the degree of polarization in the copper ion deposition process increases rapidly. As the amount of the additive increases, this polarizing effect becomes more pronounced. Once the concentration of PDS reaches 50 mg/L, further increases in the additive do not significantly enhance the polarizing effect, indicating that the leveling action of PDS has reached its limit at this concentration. Even at a PD concentration of 100 mg/L, the anodic stripping coulombs remain lower than those of PDS, indicating that its inhibitory ability is weaker. text: At 500 s, when 100 mg/L of PDS is added to the solution, the potential in the VMS instantaneously drops to −0.72 V. As the solution system is stirred, the potential slowly rises, which is due to the gradual even distribution of the additive in the solution and the stabilization of the system. As indicated by Curve 1, when 20 mg/L of SPS is added to the system at 1000 s, the potential of the solution rapidly rises to −0.58 V, demonstrating that SPS strongly promotes the deposition of copper ions. At 1500 s, when 100 mg/L of PDS is added to the solution, the potential drops to −0.68 V, indicating that PDS has a strong inhibitory effect on the deposition of copper ions. However, Curve 2 shows that when 100 mg/L of PDS is added to a VMS containing PEG at 1000 s, the potential of the solution actually rises. From the chronoamperometry curves, it can be observed that the addition of both PD and PDS leads to a rise in the potential of the PEG-containing plating solution. This suggests that both additives antagonize PEG and promote the deposition of Cu 2+. However, the potential increase caused by PDS is less pronounced compared to PD. Based on differential charge density calculations, PDS introduces new interaction sites without disrupting the adsorption of PEG, resulting in weaker competition with PEG. In contrast, PD simply adsorbs onto the Cu surface, disrupting the existing PEG adsorption layer.

text: When the cathodic overpotential is low, research has found that the capacitive loop of the leveling agent PDS is significantly larger compared to PD, indicating that PDS has a stronger inhibitory effect on the deposition of copper ions and can provide a better leveling performance[34]. text: When no leveling agent is added, the average copper layer thickness on both sides of the through-hole is 12.25 µm, resulting in a through hole plating TP value of only 56.61 %. After adding 10 mg/L of PDS, the average thickness of the copper layer inside the through-hole increases to 2 2.3 5 μ m, raising the TP value to 76.28 %. This represents an increase of ^ 1 9.6 7 % in the TP value. Additionally, after adding 10 mg/L of PD, the TP value increases to 60.20 %. Compared to the through-hole sample without any leveling agent, this represents a slight increase in the TP value, indicating that PD has a moderate inhibitory effect. However, the inhibitory effect of PD is less pronounced compared to PDS, which is consistent with the results of the electrochemical tests. To further determine whether the leveling performance of PDS meets the requirements, a comparison was made with a commercially available through-hole copper plating additive (Enthone ST-2000). The study found that under the same conditions, the TP value obtained with the commercial additive was 65.65 %, which did not reach the level achieved with PDS. This indicates that PDS has the potential to become a new type of copper plating leveling agent.

text: X-ray Diffraction (XRD) tests were conducted to analyze the crys tallographic structure of the copper layer surfaces plated at different PDS concentrations. The results are displayed in Fig. 11. The XRD test results show peak positions at 43.69, 50.84, and 74.53, which corre spond to the typical characteristic peaks of copper. These peaks respectively correspond to the (110), (200), and (220) crystal planes. As the concentration of PDS increases, the peak intensity of the (220) crystal plane decreases, indicating that the presence of PDS inhibits the formation of the Cu (220) crystal plane. Additionally, using the Scherrer formula, the grain size of the copper interconnect layer under the influence of varying concentrations of PDS was calculated, as shown in Table 2. After adding 5 mg/L of PDS, the grain size rapidly decreases from 63.62 to 28.39. Subsequent increases in the concentration of PDS do not result in significant changes in grain size, indicating that PDS acts to refine the grain structure.

text: 4. Conclusion
text_index: 4. Conclusion

text: This study improves the common leveling agent PD used in acid copper plating by incorporating SO_2 and investigates the leveling performance of both leveling agents through CVS, GMs, EIS testing, and more. The introduction of the −-S0_2 structure effectively enhances the leveling capability of the leveling agent and creates new active sites on the Cu surface. The enhancement of leveling capabilities by the intro duction of the -s0_2 structure was further substantiated through differential charge density calculations. Additionally, electrochemical experiments confirmed that the optimal concentration for both PD and PDS is 100 mg/L. SEM observations of the copper layers plated at this concentration revealed a significant reduction in porosity, indicating that both additive molecules effectively decrease the porosity of the plating layer. Observations from the profilometer showed that the copper layers were smoother and the crystallization more refined. This study demonstrates that the introduction of the −-SO_2 functional group into PD leveling agents significantly improves their leveling performance. Theoretical calculations reveal that the -SO_2 group enhances molecular adsorption and introduces additional interaction sites, leading to a more uniform adsorption layer and stronger inhibition of Cu ^ 2 + deposition.Furthermore, comparative experiments show that the SO_2^- modified PD exhibits superior leveling efficiency and deposit uniformity compared to commercially available leveling agents. These findings highlight the potential oη-SO_2 modification as a novel approach for designing next-generation copper plating additives.
